title: Modern Physics 2026-1
text:
Interesting Readings

1900–1925: The Breakdown of Physics, Prof. Roman Castañeda — Historical overview of the scientific revolution that led to modern physics and quantum mechanics.
James Jeans’ Almost-Atomic Theory — A historical article discussing James Jeans’ early ideas about atomic structure before Bohr’s model.
The Quantum Theory of Radiation — Albert Einstein (1917) — Einstein’s foundational paper introducing the concepts of spontaneous and stimulated emission.
On the Imaginable Content of Quantum Theoretical Kinematics and Mechanics — Werner Heisenberg (1927) — Original work presenting the uncertainty principle and the conceptual foundations of quantum mechanics.
The 1919 Measurement of the Deflection of Light — Historical review of the famous eclipse experiment that confirmed Einstein’s general relativity.

title: Modern Physics 2026-1

Reference Textbook
The course follows the textbook Modern Physics (3rd Edition) by Raymond A. Serway, Clement J. Moses, and Curt A. Moyer as the main reference for lectures, derivations, and problem-solving activities.

About Me
I am a physics engineer and professor working in optical instrumentation, computational imaging, and applied physics. I currently serve as Full Professor at Universidad EAFIT, where I teach undergraduate and graduate courses in physics, optics, and engineering, and coordinate the Master’s program in Applied Physics.
I have also taught at Universidad Nacional de Colombia as a Graduate Teaching Assistant (Monitor Académico de Posgrado), leading theoretical and laboratory sessions in electromagnetism, digital electronics, and microcontrollers.
Additionally, I served as Full-Time Professor at Instituto Tecnológico Metropolitano (ITM), teaching courses in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and computer vision.
